issues.legal_issue: The general limitation rule for applications applies to applications under special laws when they are made to a civil court and no other limitation period is prescribed.
material_facts: An application seeking enhanced compensation for damage caused by the removal of trees was filed before a District Judge under the Telegraph Act.

The Telegraph Act referred compensation disputes to the District Judge for judicial determination, and its provisions concerning payment into court, court fees and process indicated that the District Judge acted as a civil court.
No other limitation period was prescribed for the application, which was filed more than three years after notice of the compensation assessment.
issues.conclusion: The application fell within Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963, and was barred because it was filed after three years. The Court allowed the appeal and set aside the High Court’s judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(b), 2(j), 3, 4 and 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963, read with Article 137, show that the limitation schedule covers applications, including petitions, made to courts; Article 137 is not confined to applications under the Code of Civil Procedure. The Court relied on Nityananda M. Joshi v. Life Insurance Corporation of India in distinguishing applications to tribunals from applications to courts, and on Sha Mulchand & Co. Ltd. v. Jawahar Mills in considering the earlier construction of Article 181. It disagreed with the two-Judge decision in Town Municipal Council, Athani v. Presiding Officer, Labour Court, Hubli insofar as that decision confined Article 137 to applications under the Code. Under Sections 10, 16(3), 16(4) and 34 of the Telegraph Act, read with Section 3(15) of the General Clauses Act, the District Judge acts as a civil court in deciding the compensation dispute; the Court also relied on National Telephone Co. Ltd. v. The Postmaster-General for the principle that a matter referred by statute to a court of record is determined by it as a court absent a contrary indication.

rule.if: application_proceeding and application_made_under_special_law and application_made_to_civil_court and no_other_limitation_period

predicates.application_proceeding: The proceeding is an application or petition whose timeliness is disputed.
predicates.application_made_under_special_law: A person filed the application under a special law.
predicates.application_made_to_civil_court: The application was made to a body acting as a civil court in judicially determining the matter.
predicates.no_other_limitation_period: No other limitation period is prescribed for the application.

issues.definition: When a disputed application under a special law is made to a civil court and no other limitation period is prescribed, the application is subject to the general application limit.
